title: Puto: Fluffy Steamed Coconut Rice Cakes
summary: Light, domed rice cakes made with coconut milk and steamed in paper cases until soft and fluffy.
equipment: steamer (bamboo steamer over a wok, or a steamer insert)
16 paper cases in small metal or silicone moulds (about 60 ml)

ingredients.note: use a gluten-free one if needed

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Mix the batter
steps.text: Whisk the rice flour, sugar, baking powder, yeast and salt in the bowl. Add the coconut milk and warm water and whisk for 2 min until smooth and pourable, like a thick pancake batter.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover with the tea towel and leave somewhere warm for 1 h, until a few bubbles appear. Resting hydrates the rice flour, so the cakes are tender rather than gritty.

steps.title: Fill the cases
steps.text: Bring 5 cm of water to the boil under the steamer. Set the paper cases in their moulds and fill each three-quarters full to leave room to rise.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Arrange in the steamer and wrap the lid in the tea towel to catch drips that would pit the tops. Steam over steady high heat for 15-18 min, until risen and domed and a skewer comes out clean. Steam in batches if needed.

steps.title: Cool slightly
steps.text: Leave for 5 min before lifting the cakes out of the moulds. Serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: A common mistake is letting the water drop off the boil: steady, strong steam is what makes them dome.
Do not open the lid in the first 10 min, or they may sink.
Top up the steamer with boiling water from the kettle between batches.
Check the baking powder label if you need them to be gluten-free.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for 1 day or in the fridge for up to 3 days. Re-steam for 3-4 min to soften them again.
